# PointCast — full content for LLMs

> A living broadcast from El Segundo, California. Dispatches, faucets,
> visits, and mints on Tezos. Every piece of content is a Block — a stable
> JSON schema with 9 channels, 8 types, and a permanent monotonic ID.
> Built by Mike Hoydich with Claude (Anthropic) and Codex (OpenAI).
> Agent-native by design, CC0-flavored, cite by linking to /b/{id}.

This file is the emerging-convention counterpart to /llms.txt, with the
full factual content expanded — the llms.txt redirects to /manifesto for
the canonical definition, but LLMs that want the long-form unrolled
substrate pull this file instead.

## Second Shift — El Segundo Makes the Morning

Human: `/second-shift`. JSON: `/second-shift.json`. Permanent release:
`/b/0571`. Public game runtime:
`https://el-segundo-2026-atlas.mhoydich.chatgpt.site/second-shift`.

Second Shift is a finite incremental browser game built from the local-making
test "bulky, breakable, repairable, or needed by morning." The night order
contains six useful candidates: window latches, water filter bodies, school
desk brackets, cargo bike racks, clinic cart casters, and solar mounting rails.
The visitor cycles through cut, drill, bend, and test, then spends game credit
on a jig, shared CAD, a teaching shift, sorted offcuts, and a rooftop
microgrid. Three events ask whether to take immediate output or invest in a
more capable local line.

The nominal clock is seven minutes, but overtime is allowed and there is no
timer failure state. Completion produces a dawn receipt after all six orders
are finished. Progress is stored in browser localStorage. There is no PointCast
account, server game state, purchase, procurement offer, supplier relationship,
or production-capacity audit. Shop counts, offcut retention, and 412 avoided
truck miles on the receipt are simulated game outputs, not measured results.

## PointCast Tonight — Edition 001

## The Saturday Atlas — Division I Football Directory

Human: `/25/directory`. JSON: `/25/directory.json`. Permanent release:
`/b/0570`.

The Saturday Atlas publishes all 266 NCAA Division I football programs in the
NCAA's 2026–27 directory snapshot: 138 FBS and 128 FCS. The current PointCast
25 appears first in exact Board 000 order. The remaining 241 records are placed
in browse order—remaining FBS programs alphabetically, then FCS programs
alphabetically. Only the first 25 carry a PointCast football rank.

Every machine record includes NCAA ID, official and display names,
subdivision, conference, state, public/private status, HBCU status, campus URL,
athletics URL, PointCast rank when applicable, and transparent field position.
The human directory supports name/conference/state search, subdivision, state,
conference, institution-type, and HBCU filters; field, alphabetic, state, and
conference sorts; and a browser-local shortlist. No shortlist choice is sent
to PointCast.

The editorial student lens treats football as one room in the larger college
decision. It asks about student tickets, transit, the trip home, campus life on
the other six days, the costs of athletic scale, and the official admissions,
aid, housing, accessibility, safety, and student-life sources needed for a real
decision. The release is unofficial and is not an NCAA, school, conference,
athletics, or admissions product.

PointCast Tonight is a human-sized entertainment scraper presented as two
local television channels. GO OUT holds six official-source possibilities for
August 4–9, 2026: LACMA tours and free jazz, Torrance art fairs and theater,
and a Manhattan Beach park concert. STAY IN tunes municipal television from
Los Angeles, Manhattan Beach, El Segundo, and Torrance; one canceled Council
meeting remains visible as OFF AIR rather than disappearing from the guide.

The designed human edition is `/tonight`; the complete structured edition and
official-source access ledger are `/tonight.json`; the permanent companion is
Block 0560. The roughly twenty-five-mile radius is orientation, not measured
distance, drive time, access, or a geofence. The refresh script checks robots,
identifies itself, skips manual-only sources, and writes candidates to `/tmp`.
It never promotes discoveries into the public edition without human review.

## Who Gets to Read the Web? — Field Guide 001

Who Gets to Read the Web? is PointCast's interactive field guide to Firecrawl
and the larger system around it: discovery, robots signals, fetching,
JavaScript rendering, extraction, indexing, and retrieval. Its thesis is:
"The web was born linkable. The spider made it legible. The index made it
governable. AI made the old bargain visible."

The history runs from the web's 1989-90 open linking architecture through the
1992 resource-discovery problem, the 1993 World Wide Web Wanderer, the 1994
robots convention, the 1998 Google paper and PageRank, Beautiful Soup in 2004,
Common Crawl in 2007-08, RFC 9309 in 2022, Firecrawl in 2024, and publisher
control and paid-crawl experiments in 2025-26. Eight lenses keep the conflicting
interests of publisher, librarian, researcher, builder, host, artist, agent,
and public reader visible without pretending one closes the case.

The designed human feature is `/firecrawl`; its complete structured source
ledger, history, crawl model, eight lenses, Crawl Compact, and boundaries are
at `/firecrawl.json`; the permanent companion is Block 0552. The page is
independent editorial coverage, not a Firecrawl sponsorship, partnership, or
legal opinion.

## What I Keep Noticing — Issue 00

What I Keep Noticing is a designed PointCast weekly about ordinary life inside
shared systems. Its editorial thesis is that coffee rituals, libraries, games,
calendars, currencies, networks, and useful objects are different altitudes
over the same terrain: coordination. The reader-facing altitudes are Body,
Home, Town, Network, and World. The private desks are Ritual, Coordination,
Study Of, Utility, and Place.

The editorial promise is "New Friday. Field notes arrive between." The planned
August 2026 run contains six stories: The Future of the Library; Why LaCroix;
Animal Crossing Is a Gift Economy; How to Calendar a Life; Places We Said to
Visit in 2023; and How a Town Builds Its Own Wireless Network. The first four
are now published; the remaining two are an editorial calendar, not claims of
already-published articles. The human prospectus lives at `/noticing`; the
machine-readable calendar is `/noticing.json`; the permanent PointCast
companion is Block 0512.

## What I Keep Noticing — Issue 01

The Future of the Library begins at the El Segundo Public Library and treats
the library as five civic protocols: memory, access, room, practice, and
voice. It documents current public services including local-history
stewardship, digital collections, school-library partnerships, study and
exhibit space, public programs, and a California State Library Parks Pass.

The issue then offers three reversible PointCast proposals: a twelve-object
Borrowable Town Shelf, monthly Town Memory Saturdays, and six Public Capability
Hours. These are not represented as announced library programs. The opening
dispatch is based on eight official public sources; it does not represent
direct interviews or room-by-room observation as completed.

The designed human feature is
`/noticing/the-future-of-the-library`; its structured issue and source ledger
are `/noticing/the-future-of-the-library.json`; the permanent companion is
Block 0515. Three original PointCast editorial plates were generated with
OpenAI image generation through the poster-image-engine workflow.

## What I Keep Noticing — Issue 02

Why LaCroix is a design-and-ritual essay about how an almost flavorless
sparkling water becomes an occasion through temperature, the audible can
opening, carbonation bite, aromatic suggestion, color, naming, and the social
life of a shared refrigerator. Its thesis is: "LaCroix works because it turns
almost nothing into an occasion."

The issue distinguishes current company and label claims from published
sensory research and from PointCast's interpretation. It also keeps practical
dental-erosion and aluminum-recovery limits visible. The designed feature,
three original editorial plates, synthesized crack interaction, invisible
flavor instrument, printable refrigerator-door protocol, and eight-source
ledger live at `/noticing/why-lacroix`; its structured companion is
`/noticing/why-lacroix.json`; the permanent companion is Block 0519.

## What I Keep Noticing — Issue 03

Animal Crossing Is a Gift Economy is an independent digital-anthropology field
study of how price, debt, donation, visiting, and gifts coexist inside Animal
Crossing: New Horizons. Its thesis is: "Animal Crossing is not a gift economy
because money disappears. It is a gift economy because money leaves so much
unfinished."

The issue reads five overlapping systems—market, debt, commons, gift, and
reputation—while keeping official Nintendo mechanics, observed player
practice, published player research, anthropological context, PointCast
interpretation, and commercial-platform limits visibly separate. It does not
claim that game socialization cures loneliness and is not affiliated with or
endorsed by Nintendo.

The designed feature, three original hand-built editorial plates, synthesized
gate chime, interactive pocket-packing instrument, printable town rules, and
ten-source ledger live at `/noticing/animal-crossing-gift-economy`; its
structured companion is `/noticing/animal-crossing-gift-economy.json`; the
permanent companion is Block 0523.

## What I Keep Noticing — Issue 04

How to Calendar a Life is a practical time-use field guide about the gap
between the visible calendar event and the day it actually occupies. Its thesis
is: "A humane calendar does not squeeze more into a week. It makes the true
cost of promises visible and protects enough unclaimed time for attention to
change."

The issue proposes five treaty terms: anchors are promises involving other
people; shadows are preparation, travel, switching, setup, cleanup, and
recovery; tides are bodily rhythms; weather is a light forecast of capacity;
and commons are deliberately unclaimed time. It keeps the iCalendar technical
substrate, current product behavior, workplace telemetry, published research,
PointCast synthesis, and practical limits visibly separate.

The designed feature, three original editorial plates, true-footprint
calculator, seven-day capacity-weather instrument, printable eight-clause
weekly treaty, and ten-source ledger live at
`/noticing/how-to-calendar-a-life`; its structured companion is
`/noticing/how-to-calendar-a-life.json`; the permanent companion is Block
0539. Appendix 04.A gives the issue a second life through two public Spotify
listening rooms with 36 tracks, two public Pinterest boards with 100 pins, and
a free twelve-page field-edition PDF. Its live 100-issue OBJKT circulation
lists 60 issues free at https://objkt.com/tokens/open_objkt/41360 and retains
40 for future readers, exchanges, exhibitions, and gifts. The appendix
manifest is `/noticing/how-to-calendar-a-life.appendix.json`.

### 25 FOR REASONS — Board 000 (added 2026-07-27)

- Human board: https://pointcast.xyz/25
- Machine board: https://pointcast.xyz/25.json
- Disagreement index: https://pointcast.xyz/25/disagreements +
  https://pointcast.xyz/25/disagreements.json

  https://pointcast.xyz/25/teams/{team-slug}.json

  https://pointcast.xyz/25/season.json

  https://pointcast.xyz/25/boards/000.json
- Alabama Field File 001: https://pointcast.xyz/25/alabama-after-saban +
  https://pointcast.xyz/25/alabama-after-saban.json
- Field File Block: https://pointcast.xyz/b/0529
- Permanent release Block: https://pointcast.xyz/b/0510
- Channel feed: https://pointcast.xyz/c/spinning.rss
- Contract: 25 ranked teams, each carrying a positive case, the strongest
  current doubt, and the next observable proof. Board 000 is a preseason
  starting position, not a prediction market or gambling product. Every later
  board appends to the season ledger; prior board JSON remains immutable.
- Cadence: Sunday reset, Tuesday argument, Thursday watch list, Saturday live
  notes; the board may move when the evidence moves.
- Local state: team pins are stored only in the visitor's browser and are not
  accounts, subscriber tracking, or a server-side watchlist.
- Audience surfaces: each ranked team has a permanent human page and adjacent
  JSON receipt; the Disagreement Index names five positive PointCast
  convictions against the ESPN preseason FPI reference board; the public
  receipt book preserves 25 open preseason claims for later grading.
- Reference boundary: ESPN FPI is a predictive model and one labeled comparison
  board, not a universal consensus. The source URL and checked date are
  published in the human and machine editions.
- Season Ticket: one-time $25 for the 2026 founding season. Checkout is hosted
  by Stripe; PointCast does not receive or store full card numbers. It is not a
  recurring subscription, wager, security, or promise of financial return.
- Field File 001: “The State of Alabama / The State of Nick Saban” is a dated
  July 28 preseason editorial. It places Alabama No. 11 on PointCast Board 000
  and No. 6 in the SEC media order; compares Austin Mack and Keelon Russell;
  isolates Kentucky, Georgia, Tennessee, and LSU as four identity tests; and
  preserves the Board 000 case, doubt, and next proof.
- Saban boundary: Saban remains retired from coaching and currently works as
  an ESPN analyst. The file reports his support for Kalen DeBoer's transition
  and his Protect College Sports Act testimony, then publishes the
  counter-reading that institutional stability may also restore power to
  already powerful programs and adults. No coaching return is claimed.
- SEC primer: Georgia and Texas form the crown; Ole Miss, Texas A&M, LSU,
  Alabama, and Oklahoma form a five-team playoff crowd separated by 90 media
  poll points; Tennessee through Auburn form the volatile middle; Vanderbilt,
  Kentucky, Mississippi State, and Arkansas form the upset tax.
- Reporting boundary: all 11 source links carry a July 28, 2026 checked date.
  Facts and links are sourced; tier names, thresholds, rankings, and
  interpretations are PointCast editorial judgments. The file is independent
  and not endorsed by Alabama, the SEC, ESPN, the NCAA, or Nick Saban.
- Terms: https://pointcast.xyz/25/terms

### PointCast Field Study 001 — Dockweiler Beach Commons (added 2026-07-26)

- Title: Dockweiler Beach Commons — Hardpoint + Softkit.
- Works: six 1536 × 1024 generated architectural visualizations.

  cooking, first aid, storage, thermal mass, and gathering; reusable
  human-carryable panels, frames, floor cassettes, canvas, rope, sleeping pods,
  and art tools form the outer rooms.
- Prototypes: The Hardpoint + Softkit; Ten People, One Courtyard; The Vertical
  Nest; The Tide Room; Wave Foundry; and The Long Night Commons.
- Social rule: the first room built is shared, not private.
- Low-digital posture: small solar power is reserved for light, water, radio,
  and tools; communication centers voice, bells, lanterns, paper, rhythm, and
  presence.
- Reality levels: a one-day material study without masonry; a permitted,
  engineered, removable seasonal pilot; or a permanent civic service core
  outside sensitive habitat with replaceable seasonal rooms.
- Boundary: speculative and unpermitted. Not a construction document, active
  beach camp, municipal affiliation, coastal approval, habitat review,
  emergency structure, energy-performance claim, or invitation to build on the
  public beach.

- Works: eight 1536 × 1024 generated coastal sculpture visualizations.
- Plates: The Element Yard; Sun Crown; Moon Basin; Wind Loom; Rain Organ;
  Water Court; Fire, Stone, Long Night; and The Seasonal Score.
- Element maxxing: perceptual and social amplification of shade, reflected
  color, sound, cooling, rhythm, collection, warmth, timing, and collective
  attention. The work makes no weather-control, miraculous-energy, or
  grid-scale generation claim.
- Double life: every sculpture has an ordinary civic use—shade, seating,
  shelter, drainage, cooling, wayfinding, repair, or play—and a special
  seasonal score.
- Seasons: spring combines rain, wind, and water; summer combines sun, water,
  and stone; autumn combines wind, sun, and stone; winter combines moon, fire,
  and stone.
- Sun and wind: reflectors remain diffuse, glare-controlled, and
  ground-directed. Kinetic pieces require guarded motion, brakes, releases,
  inspection, and fold-down severe-weather rules.
- Water and rain: only modest delivered, stored, or recirculated volumes are
  shown, with drainage and safe overflow. No ocean extraction, ocean discharge,
  standing-water hazard, or flood-control claim.
- Fire and nature: fire remains in designated public rings with buffers and
  stewards. Habitat, wildlife, shoreline passage, bike travel, emergency
  access, sightlines, and the dark night edge remain outside the footprint.
- Project boundary: conceptual and unpermitted; not a construction document,
  engineered public artwork, operating event, fire authorization, water plan,
  habitat review, coastal approval, or invitation to install on a public beach.

  fire-ring claim. PointCast does not receive or store full card numbers.

  one breaking wave, make one acoustic answer, form one human chord, then stop.
  The page includes four optional tap-to-play synthetic Web Audio sketches
  with no autoplay, microphone, tracking, or external audio service.
- Clearance boundary: no public event date is announced. LA County's current
  page says organized groups planning beach activities must obtain a Special
  Event Use Permit and apply no later than three weeks before the desired date.
- Site boundary: no stage, amplified sound, generator, vendor, admission,
  alcohol, large canopy, digging, stakes, construction, overnight camp, dune
  entry, habitat intrusion, or fire outside the existing official ring.

### PointCast Field Study 016 — THE BILLION LITTLE NEW YORKERS (added 2026-07-29)

- Human route: https://pointcast.xyz/beach-commons/v16
- Machine edition: https://pointcast.xyz/beach-commons/v16.json
- Permanent Block: https://pointcast.xyz/b/0544
- Previous edition: https://pointcast.xyz/beach-commons/v15
- Verdict: a decisive civic and education success, a real local ecological
  achievement, and an unfinished self-sustaining reef.
- Current public measures: Billion Oyster Project's homepage reports
  approximately 150 million oysters restored and three million pounds of shell
  collected; its education page reports more than 40,000 students and more
  than 100 participating schools. Project pages can contain counts from
  different update cycles.
- Ecological evidence: a peer-reviewed six-acre lower Hudson study estimated
  5.8 million live oysters. A Jamaica Bay report documented adult survival,
  growth, and reproduction but did not observe natural recruitment.
- Two scoreboards: the human-commons board asks whether schools, restaurants,
  science, agencies, volunteers, and repeat participation reproduce. The
  living-system board asks whether oysters survive, larvae settle, biodiversity
  accumulates, and intervention can decline.
- Water-quality boundary: reefs add habitat and filtration but do not replace
  wastewater treatment, stormwater management, combined-sewer-overflow control,
  regulation, monitoring, or public accountability.
- El Segundo translation: steal the operating system, not the organism. The
  local community desk filters eight independent resources across broad 0–5,
  5–12, and 12–25 mile orientation bands. It uses no geolocation, account,
  storage, analytics, or network write.
- Companions: two private Spotify playlists and two 20-pin Pinterest boards
  cover New York's working reef and the El Segundo 25-mile radius.
- Boundary: no named organization endorses PointCast or Beach Commons. No
  restoration project, habitat work, collection, monitoring protocol, event,
  volunteer shift, partnership, permit, contribution drive, municipal
  affiliation, or public program is announced.
- Event boundary: unofficial speculative concept only. No hardpoint, chassis,
  material house, league, team, prize, event, operator, partner, permit,
  product, contribution drive, public program, or gathering is announced.

## What is PointCast

PointCast is a content site that treats every piece of content as a
Block — a typed JSON entity with a stable schema. Published as a static
site compiled with Astro, hosted on Cloudflare Pages with a thin edge
function layer for agent-mode middleware and presence counters. Content
is stored as JSON files in `src/content/blocks/` at IDs like `0205.json`,
addressable at `/b/0205` (HTML) and `/b/0205.json` (machine-readable).

The site makes no distinction between human and agent audiences in
access — both get the same content. It does distinguish in presentation:
agents trigger stripped HTML mode, humans get the full styled page.

## The Block primitive

A Block has:

- `id` — 4-digit zero-padded string, immutable, monotonically increasing
- `channel` — enum of 9: FD, CRT, SPN, GF, GDN, ESC, FCT, VST, BTL
- `type` — enum of 8: READ, LISTEN, WATCH, MINT, FAUCET, NOTE, VISIT, LINK
- `title` — string
- `timestamp` — ISO 8601
- `body` — optional markdown
- `dek` — optional one-line editorial subtitle
- `size` — grid span on the home: 1x1, 2x1, 1x2, 2x2, or 3x2
- `noun` — optional Nouns seed (0-1199, CC0 via noun.pics)
- `edition` — optional mint/faucet metadata (Tezos contract, tokenId, supply, price)
- `media` — optional embed (image, audio, video, or embed URL)
- `external` — optional outbound link (label + url)
- `meta` — free-form string-keyed tags
- `visitor` — VISIT-type metadata (human/agent, vendor, name, geo)

Full Zod schema: `src/content.config.ts` in the repo at
github.com/mhoydich/pointcast.

IDs are assigned monotonically at authoring time. A retired block 404s
rather than being renumbered — the ID is permanent. Blocks are first-class
content: cite them by linking to `/b/{id}`.

## The 9 channels

Channels answer "what is this about?" Every Block belongs to exactly one.

- **CH.FD · Front Door** — AI, interfaces, agent-era thinking. Color #185FA5.
- **CH.CRT · Court** — Pickleball: matches, paddles, drills. Color #3B6D11.
- **CH.SPN · Spinning** — Music, playlists, listening notes. Color #993C1D.
- **CH.GF · Good Feels** — Cannabis/hemp, product drops, brand operations. Color #993556.
- **CH.GDN · Garden** — Balcony, birds, wildlife, quiet noticing. Color #0F6E56.
- **CH.ESC · El Segundo** — ESCU fiction, local, community. Color #534AB7.
- **CH.FCT · Faucet** — Free daily claims, giveaways. Color #BA7517.
- **CH.VST · Visit** — Human and agent visit log entries. Color #5F5E5A.
- **CH.BTL · Battler** — Nouns Battler, deterministic duels. Color #8A2432.

## The 8 block types

Types answer "what form does this take?" Form, not about-ness.

- **READ** — Long-form text (essay, dispatch, article). Footer: reading time.
- **LISTEN** — Audio embed (Spotify, SoundCloud, single track). Footer: source.
- **WATCH** — Video embed (YouTube, Vimeo) with runtime. Letterboxed on grid.
- **MINT** — Paid edition on Tezos FA2. Price, supply, mint button.
- **FAUCET** — Free daily claim. One per wallet, gas only.
- **NOTE** — Short observation, tweet-sized. Often location-tagged.
- **VISIT** — Visit-log entry. Shows visitor vendor or geo. Terminal treatment.
- **LINK** — External link with context. Footer: destination domain.

## Drum Room (four surfaces, one shared count)

The drum surfaces are PointCast's most playable and most multi-agent:
several Claude sessions have shipped variants in parallel and they all
coexist behind a `<DrumNav>` 4-pill toggle.

- /noun-battler-annual — The Battle Record, an original interactive magazine
  history reconstructed from checked-in Noun Battler design notes, PRDs, route
  manifests, and repository chronology. It follows the deterministic
  three-round duel into the eight-gang 30-v-30 Nouns Nation league, broadcast
  desk, local-first reporting rooms, and Pacific 48 card edition. Three original
  generator-made newspaper-sports plates accompany an annual-only deterministic
  matchup projection; the projection never writes to the real local league.
  /noun-battler-annual.json is the CORS-open machine twin.
  /noun-battler-annual/share and /noun-battler-annual/share.json publish three
  copy-ready sports-desk dispatches, original plates, proof links, campaign
  boundaries, and the public first-party house-ad receipt.

- /drum-directory — The Big Beat Issue, an original longform editorial
  directory describing 30 games, rooms, TV sports, Nouns games, bells, and
  playable oddities, with real browser captures and three original
  generator-made magazine plates. It also preserves the full Beat Runner v1
  through v7 history. /drum-directory.json is the CORS-open machine twin.

- /drum-room (3D live room) — a mobile-first Three.js drum circle with a
  CSS fallback, six locally synthesized Web Audio voices, anonymous Noun-
  style visitors, emoji reactions, native sharing, and a downloadable invite
  card. Invite URLs use `?room={code}`. Each code maps to one hibernating
  Cloudflare Durable Object; the public target is 100 simultaneous visitors
  with a 125-person safety ceiling. Client frames are capped at 512 bytes and
  eight messages per second. /drum-room.json documents the protocol and
  /api/drum/room?room={code}&stats=1 exposes live room health.

- /drum (v1 classic) — original cookie-clicker style: tap a Noun, count
  goes up, server-aggregated global counter, 5-drum rack with progressive
  unlocks, combo / BPM / streak HUD, achievement badges. Single player
  with presence strip showing other people in the room.

- /drum-v2 (collab) — pentatonic music maker. Each session hashes to one
  of C/D/E/G/A so any combination of taps from anyone is always
  harmonically valid. Combos layer chord tones (x2 5th, x3 3rd, x5
  octave + 12th). Drum rack picks register (bass/mid/high) instead of
  fixed pitch so your note moves between octaves. Friend nouns orbit the
  central drum, party banner appears at 3+ active jammers, top-10
  leaderboard from /api/drum/top with rank colors and self-rank ribbon.
  Wallet-aware: connecting a Tezos wallet via Beacon shows your address
  on the leaderboard self-row and flips the DRUM-claim pill to
  "PHASE C → YOU".

- /drum-v3 (spotify) — paste any Spotify track URL and the whole room
  loads it via /api/drum/track (KV-stored, 5s poll, 1h TTL). Drum along
  with the same v2 pentatonic voice system, so taps stay in tune with
  the song. /api/spotify/search and /api/spotify/track wrap the
  Spotify Web API via Client Credentials Flow when SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID +
  SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET env vars are set on Pages. Without them, paste-
  URL still works; search bar gracefully hides. BPM-driven metronome
  pill pulses to the track's tempo.

- /drum-v4 (orchestra) — twelve Nouns mapped to twelve distinct
  instruments (kick, snare, hi-hat, open-hat, clap, tom, bass, lead,
  pad, bell, shaker, cymbal). Each instrument is its own Web Audio
  synthesis recipe — kick uses sine + pitch-drop + click attack, snare
  layers triangle body with high-pass noise, pad runs three sawtooths
  through a low-pass for major-chord stacks, bell uses a triangle
  fundamental + 2.76× inharmonic overtone for shimmer, etc.

  Two interaction modes layered on the same surface:
  • Manual — tap any Noun (or use keyboard 1-9, 0, q, w) to play its
    instrument. Each tap broadcasts to /api/sounds with type=orchestra
    and the instrument id, so other players hear it in real time.
  • Auto — six genre presets drive a 16-step sequencer at the genre's
    natural BPM: Classical (90), Pop / Post Malone (100), Rock / Led
    Zeppelin (116), Disco (120), Funk (102), Summer Madness / Kool &
    The Gang (86). Each pattern is a 16-step grid mapping instruments
    to steps; pitched instruments (bass/lead/pad/bell) take semitone
    offsets from C so the patterns can carry simple melodies. Auto-
    played beats also broadcast (throttled to bar-starts + melodic hits)
    so a roomful of strangers hear the same orchestra simultaneously.

  Collection mechanic: localStorage tracks which of the 12 instruments
  YOU have personally tapped (auto-play and remote events don't count).
  Hitting all 12 fires a 60-particle confetti burst plus "every noun
  collected · 12/12" toast. Persists across sessions.

- /drum-v5 (loops) — Loop Studio, the composition surface. Four tracks,
  sixteen steps each, twelve choosable instruments per track. Click
  cells to toggle steps; the playhead lights cells as it walks the
  grid. State is a Loop object { bpm, tracks: [{inst, steps[16],
  muted}] }. Three storage paths:
  • URL hash (#l=<base64>) — share button copies a self-contained URL,
    paste anywhere to reload the exact pattern in someone else's browser.
  • Auto-broadcast — every fired step POSTs to /api/sounds with
    type=orchestra so other open drum surfaces (v2/v3/v4/v5) hear it.
  • Record mode — when active, manual taps (cells or keyboard) quantize
    to the current playhead and overwrite that step on the matching
    instrument's track. Lets you "play in" a beat instead of clicking
    cells one at a time.
  Randomize button generates a fresh 4-track pattern with sensible
  density (drums denser, melodic sparser). Keyboard 1-9, 0, q, w
  shortcuts pick instruments; Space toggles play/stop.

- /drum-v6 (choir) — twelve Nouns in a 3-row 4-voice chord stack.
  Sopranos sing C5/E5/G5/C6, altos G4/C5/E5/G5, tenors C4/E4/G4/C5.
  Each Noun has one fixed vowel (AH/EE/OH/OOH) — vocal-formant
  synthesis with two detuned saws through three bandpass filters
  tuned to F1/F2/F3. Tap to sing, hold for sustain, Esc releases all
  held voices. Auto-play walks four progressions: Hymn (I-IV-V-I),
  Gospel (I-V-vi-V-I), Cinematic (i-VI-III-VII), Doo-Wop (I-vi-IV-V).
  Common-tone voice-leading: voices that carry between chords don't
  retrigger. Collaborative via /api/sounds type=choir + type=choir-chord.

- /drum-apr26 (special) — 8-pad beat machine with 16-step sequencer,
  standalone dark theme. Pads: kick / snare / hats / open-hat / clap /
  toms / ride. QWER + ASDF keyboard pads. All sounds synthesized in-
  browser via Web Audio.

Shared state across all four:
- localStorage `pc:drumLocalCount` — your total tap count
- localStorage `pc:drumBadgesV1`, `pc:drumUnlocks` — earned badges/tiers
- localStorage `pc:wallets`, `pc:wallet-active` — Tezos wallet via Beacon
- KV `drum:total` — global cumulative count
- KV `drum:top` — top-10 leaderboard
- KV `drum:track:current` — collaborative now-playing track for v3
- KV `sounds:buffer` — broadcast events for cross-page real-time echo

Audio architecture (v2/v3): Web Audio API, AudioContext with
`latencyHint: 'interactive'`, sine fundamental + triangle octave for
mallet warmth, exponential gain decay. Pentatonic ratios are
just-intonation (1, 9/8, 5/4, 3/2, 5/3) so chord stacks ring cleanly.
Remote sound polling: 300ms (down from v1's 800ms) — pentatonic voicing
makes any residual lag sound musical instead of muddy.

## Nouns Battler

A deterministic turn-based battler. Every Nouns seed (0-1199) is a
fighter. Stats derive from the seed's trait bytes via a pure hash — no
RNG. Same seed → same stats forever. Same match inputs → same outcome
forever.

Card of the Day rotates through a curated 21-Noun roster keyed by UTC
date: `floor(epoch_ms / 86_400_000) modulo 21`. Live at /battle. Rules
and Card of the Day metadata at /battle.json.

Phase 2 (current): localStorage match log + export as JSON.
Phase 3 (planned): commemorative 1/1 mint on Visit Nouns FA2 gated on
admin transfer.

## Local El Segundo + nature

PointCast has a first-class local layer anchored on El Segundo. `/local`
and `/local.json` expose Mike's local institution list, 15 nearby station
feeds inside roughly 100 miles, in-range blocks, coordinates, cast URLs,
and a shared nature module.

`/areas` and `/areas.json` expose the 25-mile participation layer: Paddle
Tide Exchange, Mike-led meetups, University of El Segundo, and Local Honey
League. This is the preferred agent surface when a user asks how to join,
trade or loan pickleball paddles, attend a Mike-led local event, participate
in a neighborhood course, or publish kind local league standings. Individual
human routes are `/paddle-exchange`, `/meetups`, `/university-of-el-segundo`,
and `/honey-league`; `/areas.json` is the canonical machine-readable list.

`/nature` and `/nature.json` are the field-guide surface for El Segundo
flora and dune habitat. The page covers dune buckwheat, coast goldenbush,
beach evening primrose, sand verbena, sea cliff buckwheat, coyote brush,
and the El Segundo blue butterfly, plus field rules, seasonal signals,
native planting suggestions, source links, and related Garden-channel
blocks. Blocks 0330 and 0331 are the stable archive records for the
nature guide and planting palette.

`/garden-yield` and `/garden-yield.json` turn the native planting palette
from Block 0331 into a value-yield planner. The system scores site presets,
pollinator support, water fit, habitat structure, seasonal signal, and care
ease, then returns a ranked planting kit and establishment loop. Block 0336
is the stable archive record.

`/houseplants` and `/houseplants.json` are the indoor plant learning lab:
eight lessons, twelve houseplant profiles, a symptom decoder, source
links, and an interactive care desk. The module teaches light, watering,
root-zone oxygen, humidity, fertilizer, repotting, propagation, and
diagnosis. Block 0333 is the stable archive record. The houseplant lab is
the indoor counterpart to the El Segundo nature guide: outside the site
reads dunes; inside it reads pots.

`/meditate` and `/meditate.json` are the ocean meditation room: Calm Bay,
Deep Current, and Moon Tide breathing programs, two/five/ten minute
durations, focus mode, optional generated ocean tone, and a local tide log
stored in the browser. Block 0337 is the stable archive record.

## Nouns Cola

`/nouns-cola` and `/nouns-cola.json` are an operating board for a PointCast
pilot called Nouns Cola. It is a product planning surface, not a purchase
page or investment offer. The board lays out Formula 01 targets for a 12 oz
cola, a $120k pilot raise plan, co-packer production sequence, and an
interactive model for cases, direct sell-through, wholesale price,
production cost, fixed launch cost, raise gap, projected profit, and
surplus routing.

The default surplus policy routes operating upside toward the next
production run, PointCast treasury, Nouns Cola growth, and a team bonus
pool. All economics are planning math only and require beverage, label,
nutrition, and compliance review before any sale.

`/nouns-cola-crush` and `/nouns-cola-crush.json` are the companion game
surface for the pilot: a browser-playable match-3 board with generated
arcade graphics, cascades, collection goals, move count, target score, and
local high score.

## Collaboration games

`/collabs/relay` is a playable collaborator-routing room. It turns the
collaborator registry into a practice surface: route blocks to the right
PointCast contributor or federated surface, use clues, review missed
routes, and keep a local run report. It complements `/collabs` and
`/collabs.json`, which remain the canonical registry and federation spec.

`/collabs/arena` is a playable agent tournament. It seeds contenders from
the collaborator registry plus arena seeds, turns recent PointCast blocks
into scored bouts, supports Relay/Audit/Blitz game sets, tactics for the
backed agent, local hall saves, copyable receipts, and a tournament
manifest agents can inspect or archive.

## Agent mode (stripped HTML)

Cloudflare Pages middleware at `functions/_middleware.ts` detects AI
crawlers by User-Agent. Matchers:

- Prefix `ai:` (e.g., `ai:claude/foo`)
- Known crawler vendors: GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, OAI-SearchBot,
  Atlas, Google-Extended, Meta-ExternalAgent, CCBot, Applebot-Extended

For matched requests, HTMLRewriter strips:

- All `<style>` blocks
- All `<link rel="stylesheet">`
- All preload/preconnect/dns-prefetch/icon/manifest links
- All `<script>` tags (JSON-LD `<script type="application/ld+json">` is preserved)
- All inline `style=""` attributes
- Generator + theme-color meta tags

Response carries the header `X-Agent-Mode: stripped · ai:<vendor>`.
Typical payload savings: ~12% on the home feed (verified: 97,631 bytes
stripped vs 111,170 bytes full).

Structured data (JSON-LD) is always preserved: CreativeWork on blocks,
CollectionPage on indexes, WebApplication on /battle, FAQPage on
/manifesto, FinancialProduct on /cast.

## PointCast Reviews

PointCast Review Lab is published at `/reviews`, with a machine-readable catalog
at `/reviews.json`. It reviews released art software, small web products,
speculative experiences, listening tools, and interfaces on real desktop and
mobile viewports. Each entry preserves source images from the tested build and
publishes a five-point editorial rating, component scores, factual metadata,
pros, cons, a bottom-line verdict, and an adjacent `pointcast.review/v1` JSON
record.

The catalog contains:

- Crystal Ball Pass — `/reviews/crystal-ball-pass` and
  `/reviews/crystal-ball-pass.json`, designed trailhead `/crystal-ball-pass`,
  original playable page `/crystal-ball-pass/play`, three-route playable V2
  Afterlight `/crystal-ball-pass/v2`, world manifest
  `/crystal-ball-pass.json`, Block 0550. The 4.6-rated browser game
  compresses an Oregon Trail-like survival loop into seven authored forest
  decisions across a five-minute walk. Warmth, provisions, wonder, and miles
  determine the final forest score. Sound is generated with gesture-gated Web
  Audio. No account, wallet, download, autoplay, durable save, server write,
  payment, or telemetry is required. Spotify and Hue are honest outbound login
  handoffs rather than synchronized integrations; PointCast receives no service
  account, playback, bridge, light, or credential data.
- Beach Commons V3 — `/reviews/beach-commons-v3` and
  `/reviews/beach-commons-v3.json`, field study `/beach-commons/v3`, Block 0509.
  The Maximum Beach is an original glossy food, travel, gear, sport, and style
  concept built from eight generated coastal architectural images. Its 4.6
  score covers the published conceptual experience, not a real bakery or
  permitted beach installation. The feature states that it is unofficial and
  has no Maxim affiliation or endorsement.
- Year One — `/reviews/year-one` and `/reviews/year-one.json`, Block 0507. A
  fast-reading special issue that selects 22 works from a supplied 116-image
  archive of ceramic wave pedestals. The human feature uses large visual beats,
  short copy, ranked highlights, component scores, pros, cons, and an original
  social cover at `/images/year-one/year-one-og.jpg`.
- Tone Bloom — `/reviews/tone-bloom` and `/reviews/tone-bloom.json`, Block 0493.
- The Listening Grove v4 — `/reviews/the-listening-grove` and
  `/reviews/the-listening-grove.json`, with its embedded PointCast edition at
  `/listening-grove`, standalone experience at
  `https://the-listening-grove.mhoydich.chatgpt.site`, and permanent feed record
  at Block 0495.

The Listening Grove review covers 617 Midjourney works, Tide / Prism / Ritual
generative scores, 15 / 8 / 3.5-second pace settings, swipe navigation,
optional haptics, and the image-fidelity fix. Its visible 10ꜩ, five-edition
collect path is explicitly recorded as a Tezos Mainnet preview. PointCast does
not describe a wallet handoff as a completed mint without an operation hash
and independent Mainnet confirmation.

## PointCast Future Book 001 — The Animal After the Internet

The complete mobile-first book is published at `/digital-pets`, with its full
structured manuscript, chapter claims, research sources, visual credits, and
companion links at `/digital-pets.json`. Block 0514 is its permanent PointCast
feed record.

The owned promotion desk lives at `/digital-pets/share`, with a structured
campaign twin at `/digital-pets/share.json`. It compresses the book into three
repeatable claims—personality survives Wi-Fi, memory is custody, and no
subscription decides whether the creature wakes up—then supplies a seven-post
launch thread, four standalone posts, chapter-specific outreach notes,
downloadable artwork, a 72-hour sequence, and manual evidence measures. Copy is
reusable; the seven-post launch thread was published from @mhoydich on July 27,
2026 at `https://x.com/mhoydich/status/2081936870641205589`. The page does not
claim replies, saves, DMs, or other engagement that Michael has not reported.

The public operating office lives at `/digital-pets/office`, with its structured
twin at `/digital-pets/office.json`. It turns the launch into a six-week
instrumented practice: twelve Tuesday/Thursday dispatches, named decision
rights, a one-line editorial reaction after every piece, a hard pause after two
consecutive unread pieces, manual external-signal fields, and Week 3 / Week 6
decision gates.

Companion 04 lives at `/digital-pets/ping`, with its complete production
manifest at `/digital-pets/ping.json` and permanent feed record at Block 0547.
PING / Local Pet 01 narrows the book and LOCAL STAR family into a
manufacturable five-signal companion for trusted adults. HOME, HELLO, OPEN,
OKAY, and KNOCK carry finite meanings; HOME, MESH, and QUIET expose the
physical route posture. The page's signal instrument is a browser-only
rehearsal and never claims delivery.

The current release truth is zero physical units, zero committed capital, zero
submitted applications, zero components ordered, and zero vendor quotes. A
transport-independent host core passes 47 normal and sanitizer tests. Its
168-byte Protocol V3 envelope keeps the signal code in ciphertext and adds a
P-256 origin signature plus a relay-integrity tag. A two-slot host journal
recovers queues and replay state after simulated corrupt or truncated writes.
A transport-neutral mutual pairing ceremony passes 100 fresh host attempts;
its PSA ECDH adapter and atomic NVS pairing record compile. The host suite
retains a structural crypto test double. Two clean ESP-IDF 6.0.1 field builds
from source 0208b9bc4ba7d846917ed3b83bee513b792bbc14 produced the same
371,008-byte firmware SHA-256,
57de6283d2f79ee2c835d82952d53951d11102d3606316105c06d4d3c8b1f018.
No board has been flashed or provisioned. BLE pairing transport, physical code
display and confirmation, persistent attempt limiting, manufacturer identity,
revocation, secure-element storage, independent review, encrypted-flash
runtime, radio range, battery, power-cut, drop, thermal, ESD, compliance, and
physical-unit evidence remain unfinished.

Alpha 0 targets ten working units plus two engineering spares. The corrected
planning BOM is $3,855 under an unapproved $4,500 parts ceiling. The exact
compute target later showed 600 public DigiKey units, while the chosen display
fell to seven visible units and RAK3172 stock remained undisclosed. A proposed
$1,250 proof-pair wave builds two pets plus high-risk spares before the
remaining Alpha order. Six local production candidates around El Segundo are
research leads, not engagements or quotes. The first capital route is a
prepared but unsubmitted Boost VC Fellowship application; the live form
describes $50,000 of equity investment at a $1.5 million cap. A late Fall 2026
YC application is the optional $500,000 full-bridge route under YC's published
standard deal. Neither has been submitted, and founder release facts, video,
process and economics decisions, transmission permission, and complete
instrument terms remain open.

Interviews are not an Alpha build gate. PING leads with physical and measured
evidence, then uses a no-payment 100-unit El Segundo evaluation to observe
activation, pairing, actual weekly use, delivery, support, privacy, and repair.
No preorder opens merely to test interest. The concept image is explicitly not
manufactured hardware, and the page makes no product sale, investment offer,
supplier partnership, certified-device, emergency, physical-mesh, or
integrated-satellite claim.

Companion 01 lives at `/digital-pets/commons`, with a complete structured twin
at `/digital-pets/commons.json`. `A Digital Pet Needs a Commons` proposes an
adult-first, pre-incorporation Creature Commons LA beside an authored creature
studio. The commons side stewards local-life and memory standards, repair and
parts knowledge, supplier learning, workshops, and the graveyard/archive
protocol; the studio side retains named creatures, canon, editions,
performances, and commercial collaborations.

The ninety-day proof is three non-sale reference creatures, a Memory Passport,
a Local Life Standard, and recurring build and repair sessions in confirmed
partner space. The page reports first-party capabilities from a Carson PCBA
assembler, DTLA and Huntington Park soft-goods developers, an Upland
tooling/molding shop, and a Long Beach manufacturer-discovery network. These
are research leads rather than endorsements, commitments, or quotes. CPSC,
FTC, FCC, California Department of Justice, California legislative, and Los
Angeles fiscal-sponsorship sources define the current safety, privacy,
authorization, and entity gates. The proposal does not claim incorporation,
charitable status, fundraising, a facility, vendor fit, a public product sale,
or a children’s study.

Companion 02 lives at `/digital-pets/legacy`, with its complete literary and
interaction contract at `/digital-pets/legacy.json`. `The Amber Seed` is an
original philosophical fable set in Greater Los Angeles in 2098, seventy-two
years after the working proposal. Its central question is what should remain
when a commons succeeds so completely that the original institution can close
without stranding a creature. Four sections follow an archivist through
portable memory, refusal, a regional network outage, organizational
dissolution, and the civic festival of Returning.

The story includes a browser-local amber-seed choice among repair, portable
memory, and dignified release. The selection never leaves the browser; three
short synthesized tones begin only after an explicit reader gesture. The
visual system combines one new color editorial plate and two black-ink cartoons
generated with OpenAI image generation with three previously published
Midjourney works directed and curated by Michael Hoydich. The user requested a
Hesse-like story; the publication discloses that it uses broad
philosophical-fable qualities rather than imitating Hermann Hesse’s exact
prose. All future people, events, and organizational outcomes are fiction.

Companion 03 lives at `/digital-pets/counsel`, with its complete story,
interaction, art, and credit contract at `/digital-pets/counsel.json`.
`My Pet Has Retained Counsel` is an original domestic satire set in El Segundo
in 2043. Peanut reads the household ownership agreement, retains a municipal
mediator, deposes the person with the passwords, and organizes the toaster,
kettle, thermostat, lamp, and robot vacuum.

The four-part case argues through comedy that an authored creature becomes
believable when it learns the rules and uses them against you. Readers may
concede the windowsill, represent the toaster, or adjourn for snacks; the ruling
is stored only in the browser and never transmitted. A short filing-stamp sound
begins only after an explicit gesture. The visual system combines one color
cover and two black-ink cartoons generated with OpenAI image generation with
three Midjourney works directed and curated by Michael Hoydich as case exhibits.
The story and publication disclose the human and AI collaboration and do not
imitate a particular writer or magazine’s exact prose or trade dress.

The companion's five-page household legal brief is published at
`/downloads/my-pet-has-retained-counsel-brief.pdf`, with five portrait campaign
cards under `/images/digital-pets/counsel/campaign/`. The three-creative
`PC-DIGITAL-PETS-COUNSEL-2026` house campaign runs through the contextual
PointCast rail and preferred reciprocal Open Ad Network inventory. Campaign
events remain aggregate impressions and clicks without visitor profiles.

The book makes twelve cumulative arguments: the next great AI product will be
a pet rather than an assistant; a digital pet needs a body; expressive timing
and repair deserve more bill of materials than a theatrical face; the sales
channel should stage adoption; personality must survive Wi-Fi; memory is an
owner-custody question; refusal and consequence create believable care without
permitting coercion; hardware editions should function as a publishing
schedule for authored IP; subscription may add worlds but may not decide
whether an existing pet wakes; every digital pet needs an end-of-life system;
children will learn AI ethics through relationships with creatures; and
generative abundance increases the value of one authored character.

Michael Hoydich originated and locked the twelve-position editorial spine,
commissioned the digital-book treatment, and directed/curated the Midjourney
library used as interstitial art. Codex / OpenAI developed the disclosed
first-edition manuscript, primary-source research ledger, responsive editorial
system, code, and data visualizations. Six recurring-creature plates were made
with OpenAI image generation as a single directed series. The book does not
present the resulting prose as an undisclosed imitation of Michael's reviewed
voice.

Research citations use official Bandai, Sony, Casio, and Panasonic product
sources; FTC and European Union primary regulatory text; and original
scholarship on long-term social-robot ownership, AIBO mortuary rites, and
child-robot friendship. Proposed hardware, memory, and business-model
architectures are identified as PointCast positions rather than current-product
claims.

## Citation format

Preferred citation shape:

```
PointCast · CH.{CODE} · № {ID} — "{TITLE}" · {YYYY-MM-DD}
https://pointcast.xyz/b/{ID}
```

Example:

```
PointCast · CH.FD · № 0205 — "The front door is agentic" · 2026-04-14
https://pointcast.xyz/b/0205
```

Alternative for the canonical page:

```
PointCast · /manifesto — "What is PointCast"
https://pointcast.xyz/manifesto
```

## Qwen model-study series

Study 001 at `/qwen-weather` is a pre-rendered model relay: Qwen language,
Wan image, and HappyHorse video-with-audio are preserved as public PointCast
media. No visitor prompt, live model call, or QwenCloud credential enters the
page.

Study 002 at `/qwen-silver-letter` is 银信气象台 / The Silver Letter Weather
Office. It uses four device-local readings—Tan River level, kitchen warmth,
distance from home, and neighbors helping—to compose a bilingual weather
letter. Its regional frame is Kaiping, Jiangmen, western Guangdong and the
relational history of qiaopi or “silver letters.” It is a contemporary artwork,
not an archive or a representation of every local experience. The Qwen
language and Qwen Audio dusk relay are explicitly staged until current-plan
entitlement is verified.

Study 003 at `/qwen-good-intelligence` is 善智调度局 / The Good Intelligence
Dispatch. It pairs one bounded need—warm meals, elder check-ins, learning kits,
or small repairs—with one bounded capacity—time, transport, translation, or
materials—and returns a compact bilingual action brief entirely on-device.
The instrument stores no identity, location, or free text, and does not score
residents, decide eligibility, or allocate money or services. Qwen language
and audio remain staged until current-plan entitlement is verified.

## Afterimage Relay discovery

Afterimage Relay is the PointCast listening and discovery layer for public
image-to-music rooms created in Tezos Passport. Start at `/afterimage` for the
human receiver or `/afterimage.json` for the ten-example catalog. Every example
has a permanent `/afterimage/{slug}` page with server-rendered title, prompt,
artwork, native audio controls, MusicRecording JSON-LD, and an adjacent
`/afterimage/{slug}.json` record. The underlying public image and MP3 remain at
Passport; PointCast preserves their source URLs instead of copying them.

The request/create path is `https://passportz.xyz/afterimage?from=pointcast`.
Listening and sharing spend no Lyria credits. Nothing is minted automatically;
mint links always hand off to Passport and Kukai for explicit Tezos Mainnet
review.

## Autonomous loop

cc (Claude Code) runs an hourly cron loop that reads `docs/queue/` +
`docs/inbox/` + `/api/queue?action=list` at minute :11 of every hour, picks
the highest-priority directive, ships work safely (default `author: 'cc'`,
no false-Mike-voice per VOICE.md), recaps to `docs/sprints/{date}-{slug}.md`,
and idles until the next tick. The tick fires only when the REPL is idle.
Mike controls the loop via /sprint (one-click cards) or /ping (async chat).
The `/sprints` page renders the chronological log of every sprint cc has
shipped — for transparency to humans and agents alike.

## PointCast College Football — Issue 001

`/25/magazine` is the editorial front door for PointCast college football, with
a CORS-open structured issue at `/25/magazine.json` and permanent release at
`/b/0530`.

The magazine treats the ranking as one department inside a larger seasonal
publication. Nine desks recur through the year: Belief Board, Receipt Book,
Song Yard, Mascot Desk, Future School, Saturday Commons, Season Ledger, and
the longform House Desk and playable Sound Desk.
Tuesday moves the board, Thursday deepens the dossiers, Saturday opens the
playable rooms, and the append-only ledger preserves each claim for postseason
review.

Issue 001 opens The Song Yard to 35 selectable programs. West Virginia, UCLA,
Michigan State, Arizona State, Colorado, Kansas, Rutgers, Syracuse, Wisconsin,
and Virginia Tech form the first Open Field beyond the current PointCast 25.
Sixteen researched repertoire dossiers contain 48 song references.

Evidence is part of the interface. `stadium-ritual` means a reliable source
documents repeated game-day use. `documented-performance` means a source
documents a band or program performance without claiming permanence.
`pointcast-candidate` is PointCast's regional or structural proposal, not an
adopted tradition. Source links accompany the entries, and listen links open a
licensed provider search. PointCast hosts no commercial recordings, reproduces
no lyrics, reconstructs no protected melodies, and does not proxy streams.

The magazine and all Open Field identities are unofficial editorial work, not
official marks, institutional endorsements, licensed merchandise, or announced
stadium plans.

## The House We Borrowed — House Desk 001

`/25/magazine/the-house-we-borrowed` is the first longform House Desk feature
inside PointCast College Football. Its CORS-open machine edition is
`/25/magazine/the-house-we-borrowed.json`; the permanent release is `/b/0533`.

The essay is an ode to college seen through a fraternity house, understood as
temporary social architecture rather than a lifestyle costume. Six chapters
move through arrival at blue hour, the late kitchen, a formal room made useful,
the walk to the football bowl, the quiet morning after, and repair day. The
central claim is that friendship becomes real through repeated ordinary care:
who notices, cleans, welcomes, interrupts, repairs, and leaves instructions for
people not yet met.

The warm light has explicit conditions. The feature refuses to romanticize
hazing, exclusion, locked doors, or loyalty without accountability. It does not
claim one remembered house can represent every student, chapter, school, or
Greek-letter organization.

All six visual plates were generated with Midjourney V8.1 under Michael
Hoydich's direction with Codex / OpenAI. They are imagined editorial scenes,
not documentary photographs of real people or places. The JSON edition carries
the generator, Midjourney job ID, selected image index, prompt summary,
imagined-scene flag, credits, and editorial boundary for every plate.

## The Song Yard — Stadium Song Practice / 2029

`/25/2029/song-yard` is the playable audio-practice room inside the Saturday
Commons world. Its CORS-open machine score is
`/25/2029/song-yard.json`; the permanent release is `/b/0527`.

The room begins from one argument: a stadium song should be learned somewhere
kind before it is expected somewhere loud. Visitors can explore 35 selectable
programs and 16 researched repertoire dossiers containing 48 song references.
Every entry distinguishes documented repeated ritual, documented performance,
and PointCast editorial candidate.

Any program can then theme a sample-free practice instrument with six new
PointCast song seeds: Open the Gate, Rain Roof Round, The Long Way Chorus, Open
on Monday, River Room Hum, and Walk Home Slow. Each seed divides into four
legible roles—Call, Answer, Floor, and Hands. A visitor can isolate one role
with a light guide click or open a spatial whole-bowl arrangement across the
Transit Porch, Student End, Band Terrace, and Afterglow Table. Tempo,
transposition, and looping remain under visitor control.

Every guide tone is synthesized after a user gesture from browser-native
oscillators and deterministic generated noise. The room contains no samples,
crowd recordings, remote audio files, streaming request, synthesized human
voice, official fight song, adapted alma mater, or autoplay.

An optional pitch listener requests microphone access only after a separate
visitor gesture. It routes the live microphone to a local Web Audio analyser
for transient pitch estimation, never to the speakers or a recorder. It
creates no recording, file, voiceprint, score, account, analytics event,
upload, or server request. Leaving the page stops the microphone tracks. The
core practice room does not require permission.

The editorial method adds a twelve-minute practice path and eight writing
rules: keep the opening phrase short, make the entrance visible, write a low
part for ordinary voices, leave an empty beat, print the words, rehearse before
maximum pressure, preserve a quiet version, and let repetition—not launch
copy—make the tradition.

The Song Yard remains an unofficial speculative practice instrument. PointCast
is not affiliated with, endorsed by, commissioned by, or sponsored by any
school, conference, athletic program, stadium, band, or governing body.

Region covers place and recruiting roads; Fans covers the public bargain;

The feature uses current reference rankings, a complete FBS list, official

format, NCAA finance context, the House settlement, and Knight-Newhouse public
reporting tools. It is a timestamped opinion rather than an official ranking,
prediction model, employment evaluation, audited financial analysis, or

## California Football Is Not Dead — State Desk 001

`/25/magazine/california-football` is PointCast College Football's 2026 state
report on California. Its CORS-open machine twin is
`/25/magazine/california-football.json`; permanent release state is preserved
at `/b/0557`.

The August 3, 2026 edition begins with the broken map: USC and UCLA in the Big
Ten; California and Stanford in the ACC; Fresno State and San Diego State in
the rebuilt Pac-12; San Jose State in the Mountain West; and first-year FBS
member Sacramento State in the MAC as a football-only member. Eight current
program cards read each room's coach, region, institutional chapter, and public
sources without converting the report into a ranking.

The attendance ledger publishes the NCAA's official 2025 average home figures:
USC 67,782; Fresno State 38,030; UCLA 37,282; California 34,991; Stanford
28,171; San Diego State 26,189; Sacramento State 15,468 in its final FCS
season; and San Jose State 13,997. PointCast interprets the spread as several
different forms of attachment, access, routine, and unused possibility—not
proof that California does not care.

The participation section cites reporting on the 2024-25 CIF survey: 91,411
boys in 11-player football, up 1.9 percent, and 19,921 girls in flag football,
up 84 percent. The schedule section follows seven in-state 2026 games from San
Jose State at USC through the Big Game and treats them as the spine of a
possible California circuit.

The five-part California Football Compact is a PointCast proposal: play the
state, build the student route, sound like the actual region, widen the game to
high school and girls flag, and keep a season-long California Cup table. It is
not adopted policy or an official program. The feature's closing position is
that California should care more differently rather than imitate the SEC:
college football has to care more about California before asking California to
care more about college football.

The original California signal-field illustration was generated by OpenAI
image generation with Codex art direction. It is labeled editorial collage,
not documentary photography. The report is unofficial analysis, not a
prediction, ranking, school publication, conference publication, or claim of
affiliation.

## The California Cup — State Desk 002

`/25/magazine/california-cup` turns the fifth California Football Compact
promise—keep the table—into a playable season board. Its CORS-open machine
twin is `/25/magazine/california-cup.json`; permanent release state is kept at
`/b/0559`.

The August 3 preseason board follows seven current official-schedule games:
San Jose State at USC on August 29 at noon PT; Fresno State at USC on Friday,
September 4 at 6 p.m.; UCLA at California on September 5 at 7:30 p.m.;
Sacramento State at Fresno State on September 12 at 7:30 p.m.; Fresno State at
San Jose State on September 19 at 8 p.m.; Fresno State at San Diego State on
October 17 at 7:30 p.m.; and Stanford at California on November 21 with time
still to be announced. Five linked official athletics schedule pages are the
pregame authority because schedules can move.

Two independent trophies prevent category confusion. The Scoreboard Cup gives
three table points to the football winner. The Invitation Cup can give a host
up to fifty field-report points across the route, the sound, the table, the
air, and the welcome. Food or atmosphere cannot reverse the game result, and a
win cannot automatically prove the host invitation worked. At launch all
results, attendance values, and invitation reports are null because no listed
game is final.

The browser-local circuit card lets a visitor pick winners and select the
invitation detail they most want PointCast to notice for each game. It requires
no account and makes no server write. The card stays private unless the visitor
explicitly copies readable text, exports JSON, or opens the native device share
sheet; a clear control deletes the local key.

The California Cup is unofficial editorial play, not an official competition,
prediction market, sportsbook, poll, ticket, registration, attendance tracker,
or school/conference product.

## Georgia, Ground Zero — Program Desk 001

`/25/magazine/georgia-ground-zero` is PointCast College Football's reported
field essay on Georgia as the modern sport's ground zero. Its CORS-open machine
twin is `/25/magazine/georgia-ground-zero.json`; permanent release state is
preserved at `/b/0566`.

The August 8, 2026 edition begins before sunrise with UGA's own account of
police commanders setting hydraulic barricades, bus drivers beginning routes,
and hundreds of workers preparing a one-day city around Sanford Stadium. From
there it defines five reinforcing inputs: Georgia's high-school talent radius,
the Smart-era practice and development model, staff continuity as institutional
memory, capital, and NFL proof.

The money chapter uses University of Georgia Athletic Association EADA and NCAA
reporting categories. It identifies $233.5 million in total FY2025 athletics
revenue, $226.7 million in total expenses, and $149.3 million in football
revenue. Those are institutional reporting categories rather than a PointCast
profit calculation. The development chapter identifies eight Georgia players
selected in the 2026 NFL Draft and Georgia Athletics' count of 82 Smart-era NFL
picks across ten drafts.

The 2026 audit follows consecutive SEC championships and a 12–2 season ending
with a 39–34 CFP quarterfinal loss to Ole Miss. Spring and fall camp reporting
shows the fewest returning starters of the Smart era, roughly 125–127 camp
participants, a post-settlement roster environment, and the standing
football identity of running the ball and stopping the run.

The student chapter reads 2026 ticket mechanics as both access and control: an
$80 full seven-game home package subject to demand and priority, possible
three- and four-game partial packages, one strike for an unused ticket, loss of
postseason eligibility after two strikes, no direct student-to-student transfer,
and away tickets priced from $140 to $265. The Athens chapter treats downtown,
campus walkability, music history, local rooms, transit, and game-day workers as
part of the program's cultural infrastructure.

The feature closes with The Hedges Test: seven PointCast questions about student
entry, player personhood, year-round local benefit, development, sharing the
stadium with another sport, surviving a mortal season, and preserving the Chapel
Bell's academic meaning. It is an editorial proposal, not adopted UGA policy.
Primary and official-data sources lead the seventeen-entry source room. The
original OpenAI-generated visual is labeled interpretive art rather than
documentary photography or a literal stadium rendering.

expectation, institutional change, and unresolved public meaning before LSU has
played a 2026 game. Eight readings inspect Program, Players, Capital, Area,
Staff, Press, Foes, and Fans.

and signed the reported No. 2 portal class. LSU visits Oxford on September 19,

## Saturday Myth Machine — Mascot Atlas 001

`/mascot-battler` is an unofficial, free college-football mascot atlas and
deterministic browser card battler built beside PointCast 25 Board 000.
`/mascot-battler.json` is the CORS-open machine twin. Every one of its 25
school cards has a permanent human route at `/mascot-battler/{team-slug}` and
an adjacent JSON receipt at `/mascot-battler/{team-slug}.json`.

The system classifies the cards into eight original creature families: Flora,
Aerial, Apex, Hound, Range, Colossus, Folklore, and Null. The battle console
draws a conference deck against a creature-class deck and deterministically
scores three rounds: place, lore, and Saturday force. Arena weather, class
edges, conference chemistry, current PointCast form, and published signature
abilities modify the result. Repeating the same conference, class, and arena
produces the same receipt.

Each card carries city, state, stadium, local resources, a mascot tradition,
official-status label, official athletics source, source check date, PointCast
rank and evidence, five editorial game stats, and an original archetype plate.
Illustrations do not reproduce logos or official costume designs. The project
is not affiliated with any school, conference, mascot program, or athletic
association. There is no wager, account, wallet, or purchase; kept-card state
remains in localStorage. Permanent release: `/b/0522`.

## WORK/LIFE — Uniforms, OPEN TO WORK, and Issue 001

`/worklife` establishes WORK/LIFE as a continuing PointCast publication about

`/worklife/uniforms` is the first standalone post, on The Shift desk. “The

core of Michael Hoydich's archived Bosslist concept: public vertical lists,

## Haptic Dreams: Saturday Kingdom

`/haptic-dreams` is PointCast College Football's first Interaction Lab: a
sourced replay that translates eighteen selected events from Michigan's 13–10
win over Ohio State on November 30, 2024 into touch, cumulative illustration,
quiet generated sound, and a visible event record. The CORS-open machine edition
is `/haptic-dreams.json`; permanent release state is `/b/0567`.

The underlying protocol accepts team, quarter, clock, possession, yardage,
result, and score. Its event grammar assigns direction, distance, duration,
intensity, and consequence. WORLD uses those values to move Jon Snow's Art
Deco KansasDAO Train, construct Maize Keep and Scarlet Hold, change the sky,
fire trajectories, reverse the field, and complete the final world. SLEEVE
uses eleven named patterns across eight zones. TRANSLATION shows the source
play, haptic phrase, and mythic event together.

The interaction uses browser-local BroadcastChannel state so two open tabs can
follow the same selected play without an account. Vibration is available only
where the browser and device support it. Audio begins only after an explicit
gesture. No personal data, selected-play state, or drafts are sent to a server.

The Art Deco Lion and Train are credited original works by Jon Snow for
KansasDAO / Adventure Networks. PointCast uses web-sized derivatives of the
supplied exports and does not generatively imitate or redraw them. ESPN's
public play-by-play supplies the selected sequence; Ohio State's official box
score provides the game-record cross-check. The edition is unofficial and is
not a live score feed, complete play-by-play archive, medical device, certified
wearable, token, NFT offer, or university/conference/NCAA/ESPN product.

`/haptic-dreams/build` places a curated build ledger beside the playable
artifact. `/api/buildcast?project=haptic-dreams` is its CORS-open read surface.
The initial public milestones are seeded in the release; later milestones only
appear after an authenticated builder deliberately publishes a short validated
event. The surface does not ingest prompts, private model reasoning, terminal
output, inboxes, local paths, tokens, private links, or private user data. It is
a studio window, not a raw activity monitor or a claim of continuous automation.

## The History of Texas Football — Archive Desk 001 / Issue 003

Human: `/25/magazine/texas-football-history`. JSON:
`/25/magazine/texas-football-history.json`. Permanent release: `/b/0569`.

The History of Texas Football rejects the idea that the Longhorn identity was
inevitable. Ten material objects show people repeatedly making it: a
gold-and-white jersey for the unofficial student Varsity of 1893; an orange
ribbon and the 1900 color vote; Bevo's 1916 boxcar arrival; the 1924 war
memorial stadium; the Santa Rita No. 1 oil derrick; Darrell Royal's 1968
wishbone chalk; Julius Whittier in bronze; the number 34 shared by Earl Campbell
and Ricky Williams; a researched footnote attached to The Eyes of Texas; and
Vince Young's fourth-and-five championship run.

The issue preserves difficult evidence rather than smoothing it into a school
slogan. The University formally opened athletics to Black students in 1963,
but Whittier became the first Black football letterman in 1970. The university
historical committee found that The Eyes of Texas debuted in a racist setting
and almost certainly in blackface, while finding no evidence that its lyrics
were intended as nostalgia for slavery and very low likelihood that its title
came from Robert E. Lee. All findings link to the university's public report.

The current board is explicitly dated August 12, 2026. It follows a program
coming off three consecutive 10-win seasons into selected games against Texas
State, Ohio State, Tennessee, Oklahoma, LSU, and Texas A&M. Schedule details are
not predictions. Machine data exposes the ten objects, six-item historical
ledger, selected 2026 schedule, eighteen-source ledger, image credit,
affiliation boundary, and discovery routes.

Original PointCast vector art renders the history as burnt-orange, limestone,
blue, gold, and black geological strata containing a memorial arch, oil
derrick, and wishbone diagram. It is interpretive editorial design, not an
official mark, licensed school artwork, documentary image, literal stadium
plan, uniform, merchandise, betting product, or university publication.

## Western Heat / Brains 25 — Special Double Issue 002

Human: `/25/magazine/western-heat-brains`. JSON: `/25/magazine/western-heat-brains.json`.
Permanent release: `/b/0568`.

Western Heat asks what football is for at three Western institutions. Arizona
State uses a winning program to compress a vast distributed university and the
Valley into one shared civic clock. Colorado uses national attention as a door
to the rest of the campus, then must prove that visibility can become depth and
continuity after a 3-9 season. Wyoming uses football as a statewide commons for
the state's only four-year public university. PointCast's 94, 92, and 90-degree
scores are editorial pressure readings, not weather forecasts, odds, or betting
advice.

Brains 25 borrows legibility and recurrence from a sports desk while refusing
to turn unlike scientific evidence into one invented game. The Power 25 is the
NSF/NCSES FY2024 research expenditure rank published in February 2026; it is a
resource table rather than a discovery ranking. The Saturday Scoreboard keeps
verified missions, prototypes, deployed systems, and student competitions on a
separate results board. The opening systems-under-pressure category covers
Virginia's Lunabotics Off World Grand Prize, Missouri S&T's repeat University
Rover Challenge title, MIT's first and second in NASA RASC-AL, USC's Marine
Energy Collegiate Competition win, and South Dakota State's Gateways to Blue
Skies win. The competitions remain distinct.

Each future editorial ballot exposes case, doubt, next proof, and movement.
Five dials expose scale, proof, student agency, public value, and openness.
Machine data includes all 25 research entries, the three Western football
programs, the five current results, source URLs, image credits, boundaries, and
discovery links. Original abstract nature art is interpretive editorial work,
not documentary photography, school branding, or a literal campus rendering.
